name: TestLPSSuite/TestProfile
statusMessage:
timed out after 5m0.001094485s (excluding download) waiting for app "4c57dcb4-9f55-4c40-ac68-63f59347cf6b" (lps-app) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: CREATING_VOLUME)

Claude's conclusion:
Confirmed: four concurrent `extract-*` snapshots are still `Active` (uncommitted) on the device at 05:57:23, well past the 5-minute timeout, with the volumes directory empty — classic concurrent-unpack contention, not a single app. This matches all the live evidence.

**Root cause:** `lps-app`'s root volume is still stuck in `CREATING_VOLUME` (live `AppInstanceStatus` shows `State:109`) well past the 5-minute deadline, with live `ctr snapshots ls` showing four concurrent `extract-*` containerd snapshots still `Active`/uncommitted — multiple container-image unpacks competing for CPU at once. Live `nproc`/`vmstat`/`uptime` on `edge-dev` show the classic oversubscription signature: the guest exposes only `nproc=1` against a device configured for 4 vCPUs, load average 5.65 right after an 8-minute-old boot, and `vmstat` shows a process perpetually blocked on I/O (`b=1`, `wa`≈21-29%). `evetest broker status` corroborates this: the Proxmox host (`farfalle`) is running 13/16 VMs at 102% of host RAM assigned, with 1.9 GiB of swap in use and host load 7.2-8.2.

This is the identical root cause as the 2026-11-21 (run #35) occurrence of this exact test (`TestLPSSuite/TestProfile`), where the ledger records `lps-app`'s unpack taking ~2m32s amid concurrent volume creates and finishing just ~15s past the deadline — the same "slow-but-completing unpack under CPU oversubscription" pattern. It is also part of a much broader, heavily recurring class (concurrent container-image unpacks exceeding the fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`→RUNNING timeout under host CPU/IO oversubscription) that has hit dozens of different tests/suites in nearly every nightly run since at least 2026-11-20 — an infrastructure/environment issue, not a product regression. No PR diff was provided for this investigation.

### Root cause

Live inspection confirms `lps-app`'s volume (`11d000d6-...`) entered `CREATING_VOLUME` at 06:13:08, with `volumemgr.CreateVolume` firing at 06:13:09.962 and not completing (`createContainerVolume ... DONE`) until 06:15:42.119 — a ~2m32s unpack that pushed the app past the 5-minute (excluding-download) deadline, which fired at 06:15:27, by only ~15 seconds. Device logs show this unpack running concurrently with at least three other volumes (`app-profile-1`, `app-profile-2`, and an `ubuntu-ctr` volume) that were also mid-`CreateVolume` in the same window and didn't finish until 06:16:39–06:16:41, i.e. multiple container-image unpacks were competing for CPU simultaneously. The device is configured with 4 vCPUs while the underlying physical host has only 2 cores (`nproc`), and the device itself showed load average 6.23 right after boot — matching the CPU-oversubscription signature. Despite the test failure, `lps-app` actually did progress and reach `RUNNING` shortly after (bootTime ~06:15:47, confirmed via live `app-info`), confirming this was a slow-but-completing unpack, not a true hang. This is the same recurring root cause documented five times in last night's ledger (2026-11-20, run #30 — `TestLocalNI`, `TestMoveAppBetweenNIs`, `TestLimitedIPSpace`, `TestFlowLog`, and a fifth `app1` case): host-resource oversubscription causing concurrent container-image unpacks to occasionally exceed the test's fixed 5-minute `CREATING_VOLUME`/RUNNING timeout. This is the first time it's been seen specifically in `TestLPSSuite/TestProfile`, but it's the same known, recurring infrastructure-level issue, not a new bug.
